activities.anchor: will shortly prove that part of Earth's core is liquid
activities.caption: P or S — file each wave fact
activities.name: eiWaveSort

config.prompt: The two body waves — file each fact:

items.label: a push wave — compression running down a Slinky
a shear wave — a flicked rope's wiggle
needs a material that can spring back sideways

config.why: One difference does all the work: P passes through liquid, S does not — which is how a ring of silence on the far side of a quake proved the outer core liquid.

activities.anchor: The coolest place on the whole journey is where you are
activities.caption: place the geotherm's endpoint
activities.name: eiGeothermPlace

config.prompt: The geotherm runs from ~15 °C at your feet to the centre — place the inner core's temperature on the scale.
config.why: About 5,400 °C — roughly the temperature of the Sun's visible surface, and solid anyway: pressure, not temperature alone, decides state.

activities.caption: stack the mechanical layers by depth
activities.name: eiLayersOrder

config.prompt: The mechanical Earth, top to bottom — order the zones:
items: Lithosphere — crust plus topmost mantle, the rigid plates
Asthenosphere — ~100–250 km, near its melting point, the low-velocity zone
Mesosphere — below 660 km, solid and too strong to break
Outer core — liquid iron, churning out the magnetic field
Inner core — solid iron from 5,150 km, crushed past melting
config.why: Two slicing schemes, one planet: the chemical layers (crust, mantle, core) overlap but do not match the mechanical ones — behaviour depends on pressure and temperature, not just ingredients.

activities.anchor: a discovery made from a single Danish station and superb reasoning
activities.caption: pair each detective with their find
activities.name: eiDetectiveMatch

config.prompt: The layer boundaries were won by listening — pair each with the discovery:

pairs.right: the Moho — waves that dove into faster rock beat the direct route; the crust's base
the core–mantle boundary near 2,890 km, fixed by the S-wave shadow zone
a solid inner core, from faint echoes inside the P-wave shadow
the CT-scan trick imaging sinking slabs and rising plumes in 3-D

config.why: No drill has passed ~12 km — everything below is known the way doctors know hearts: by listening.

activities.anchor: Continents were not ploughing through anything
activities.caption: bet before the reveal — the ridge's magnetic signature
activities.name: eiStripesPredict

config.q: New seafloor cools through reversals of Earth's magnetic field as it spreads. What pattern should the seafloor show on either side of the ridge?
choices: One wide band of a single polarity, ageing outward
Symmetrical stripes mirroring the ridge — polarity flipping outward in step
config.why: Symmetrical stripes — the tape-recorder record (Vine and Matthews, 1963) that showed new floor forming at the ridge and spreading both ways, supplying Wegener's missing engine.

activities.anchor: the one place you can walk on it
activities.caption: call the Atlantic's pace
activities.name: eiAtlanticEst

config.prompt: At divergent boundaries the seafloor welds on and spreads — roughly how fast does the Atlantic widen?
config.why: A couple of centimetres per year — the rate your fingernails grow; Iceland straddles the ridge, and the East African Rift is the same process starting on land.
config.context: Mantle rises beneath the thinning plate and melts by decompression, welding new basalt onto both plates.

activities.anchor: still rising as India continues its 50-million-year collision with Asia
activities.caption: true or false — convergent outcomes
activities.name: eiConvergentJudge

statements.s: Where an ocean plate meets a continent, the ocean plate subducts beneath.
statements.why: The Peru–Chile trench and the Andes — the descending slab's water drives the volcanism above.

statements.s: Continent–continent collision sinks one of the plates deep into the mantle.
statements.why: Neither can sink far: the crust crumples and thickens — the Himalaya.

statements.s: Challenger Deep, nearly 11 km, sits at a transform boundary.
statements.why: It is subduction — ocean meeting ocean, the older diving beneath, building island arcs like Japan and the Marianas.

statements.s: Almost all magma is born in or just above the asthenosphere.
statements.why: That rock is nearest to melting and needs only a nudge — added water or reduced pressure — to liquefy.

activities.anchor: they also provide the reference frame
activities.caption: plume meets plate — drag the divider
activities.name: eiPlumeCompare

config.prompt: A hot spot's output depends on the plate above — drag between the cases:

before.label: Plume under a moving plate
before.text: An age-progressive chain: Hawaii's 6,000 km trail, ages marching northwest to tens of millions of years old — the plate's motion recorded in rock.

after.label: Plume under unusual crust
after.text: Yellowstone: a continental hot spot that left a chain of calderas across Idaho. Iceland: a plume sitting fortuitously on a ridge, doubling the volcanism.

config.why: Plumes burn a hole a volcano at a time while plates glide over them — nearly-fixed points that make plate motion measurable at all.
